He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]]. ==Early life and career== Sochan was born in the United States, in [[Guymon, Oklahoma]]. His mother Aneta was a Polish basketball player who went there to study. In Oklahoma, she met Sochan's father, Ryan Williams, who is American. Sochan spent most of his childhood in [[Milton Keynes]], England, where he took his first steps in basketball.[https://sport.tvp.pl/52409650/eleurobasketu-do-kadry-trafil-dzieki-mamie-jeremy-sochan-niedlugo-sprobuje-zaspiewac-mazurka-dabrowskiego El. EuroBasketu: do kadry trafił dzięki mamie. Jeremy Sochan niedługo spróbuje zaśpiewać "Mazurka Dąbrowskiego"] Jakub Kłyszejko (''Sport.TV.PL''), 20 February 2021. Accessed 23 February 2021.{{in lang|pl}} Sochan began his high school career at [[La Lumiere School]] in [[Indiana]], but due to the COVID-19 pandemic, he left America. Sochan committed to playing college basketball for [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] in July 2020.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=FIBA U16 standout Jeremy Sochan commits to Baylor |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29474731/fiba-u16-standout-jeremy-sochan-commits-baylor |access-date=September 16, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=July 16, 2020}} ==College career== On January 8, 2022, Sochan sprained his ankle during a game against [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] and missed several games.{{cite news |last1=Werner |first1=John |title=Cold start costs No. 1 Bears in 61-54 loss to Oklahoma State |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/cold-start-costs-no-1-bears-in-61-54-loss-to-oklahoma-state/article_0bc498da-7671-11ec-8a0d-17a637b80c92.html |access-date=January 17, 2022 |work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |date=January 15, 2022}} Following the season, he earned the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Sixth Man Award and was named to the Big 12 All-Freshman Team.{{cite web|title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced|url=https://big12sports.com/documents/2022/3/6//All_Big_12_Release_21_22_.pdf|date=March 6, 2022|accessdate=March 30, 2022}} His team would later get a #1 seed in the [[2022 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]], but lose in the second round. As a freshman, he averaged 9.2 points, 6.4 rebounds and 1.3 steals per game. On April 15, 2022, Sochan declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web|title=Jeremy Sochan, Baylor men's basketball freshman, entering NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33742913/baylor-freshman-basketball-player-jeremy-sochan-entering-nba-draft|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|date=April 15, 2022|accessdate=April 15, 2022}} == Professional career == ===OrangeAcademy (2020—present)=== In 2020, Sochan joined the [[Germany|German]] club [[OrangeAcademy]] of the [[ProB]]{{cite web|title=Jeremy Sochan wird ein Ulmer Der MVP der FIBA U16 EM 2019 (Division B) wechselt aus den USA an die Donau|language=DE|url=https://orangeacademy.one/news/jeremy-sochan-wird-ein-ulmer-785|date=July 7, 2020|website=orangeacademy.one|access-date=July 7, 2020}} ==National team career== Sochan had represented Poland nationally at the junior level. As part of [[Poland's under-16 national basketball team]], he led his team to the title at the [[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship Division B]] in Montenegro. There, he became tournament [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]].[https://www.swp.de/sport/mehr-lokalsport/ulm/basketball-ulm-hat-zwei-neue-basketball-nationalspieler-55333437.html Ulm hat zwei neue Basketball-Nationalspieler] Sebastian Schmid ([[Südwest Presse]]), 26 February 2021. Accessed 28 February 2021.{{in lang|de}} Sochan has been a member of the [[Polish national basketball team]]. In his first game at the [[EuroBasket 2022 qualification]], he led Poland over [[Romania national basketball team|Romania]] 88–81 when he became the youngest player to ever play for Poland.
